These past few days, after submitting my PhD thesis for examination, I have been reflecting on the whole process, and come up with a few takeaways...

My five-year-old son came with me to submit my PhD thesis to the graduate office. Things went full circle as he was also there the first time I reported my arrival to the uni (he was a tiny toddler then!)

Congratulations! A lot of people have told me I'm crazy to do a PhD with a kid in tow. But my child keeps me going and gives me purpose, because I am trying to set an example on resilience for him. I am happy to see other #academicmom out here! Well done you!

Tomorrow is my last day in this office! Desk looking pretty empty. PhD thesis handed in a couple of weeks ago, been tidying up... Gearing up to move countries again while waiting for the reviewers. I feel... both liberated and sentimental?

I received some rejections, and was outright ignored by some institutions before finally being admitted to my PhD programme. It's okay to feel disappointed for a while, but it will get better! I've heard many similar stories!

I moved between countries regularly as I grew up, initially because of my parents' studies and work, and then because of my own studies. I have also chosen a career that requires me to move regularly. (1/5)

However, I feel like I don't have deep roots anywhere - too foreign-looking while abroad, too different mentally while 'home'. I'm not sure where 'home' is exactly. For now, it's wherever my family is, but they, too, move around with me. (4/5)

I've just moved back to 'home' today, and my heart aches for the previous 'home' I left behind. Not just the physical place, but also friends... At the same time, I look forward to catching up with old friends. We'll see what's in store for me! (5/5)

I am going back to government work while waiting for examiners to review my PhD thesis. I will have to do a defense later on, and anxious that I might fall out of the academic mindset. Has anyone been in a similar situation? How do you cope?
My supervisor just told me that she has all three examiners lined up for my thesis! Good to know that the review process is going to start soon, but also, OMG, I'm nervous about it. #PhD
I teared up reading this. I lost my mother when I was five. Old photographs are the only way for me to see her 😭😭😭
Bored of work; back to school!

My thesis defense, scheduled for April 1st, was always meant to be a #VirtualDefense. But I still worry whether or not it can go ahead. Feeling additional anxiety from the current global situation. #AcademicChatter

I've been dreaming about it for so long! Also, I can't afford to delay graduation, as I need my degree to actually get ahead in my career 💔 On top of everything else, this whole #COVID19 situation just adds so much stress 😔

I know there's so much going on in the world that's way more important than this, but I'd like to announce that the final amendments to my doctoral thesis have been accepted, because I am proud of this achievement. I feel bittersweet about my PhD ending 😢.

I started my PhD when my child was 2. It's doable, but you will feel more isolated (when peers went out after office hours, most days I had to rush home so my spouse could go to work). I heard a lot of people say "I don't know how you do it lol"...
...and I also felt isolated from the parents' community at kindy/school because I'd be at uni most days and hardly hung out at school. Having a supportive spouse helped a lot.
Semoga mereka semua diberikan tempat yang paling mulia di sisi-Nya. WEAR YOUR MASKS CORRECTLY AND SOCIAL DISTANCE. THE PANDEMIC IS NOT OVER.

I still remember the first session of my Academic English for International Relations class. The lecturer gave us a general topic and told us to write an essay within 45 minutes. No student was able to finish anything coherent. The lecturer then told us the importance of...
...a focused research question, reliable data and sources, and a clear argument to write a good essay. It's been 16 years since this particular class and I still remember it vividly!
